rules: PRODUCTION_SPEC §1/§3/§9; flat LIGHT backgrounds; product cut out; 1–3 words on screen; a detailed 2-D object in every shot; watermark below content; logo end card; audio LOCKED. Length 45–55 s, HARD CAP 58 s. Draw no Samsung or LG logos (text names only). Never say/show that Samsung's 'first' claim is false — only show LG's own listed '1100Hz O/C'.
official_clips: K (Samsung product page '600Hz or 1100Hz' feature clip) ≤ 3 s in scene 5; L (motion blur clip) ≤ 2 s in scene 4. Muted. Total ≤ 20 %.
palette_for_this_video: paper main; sky for speed numbers; mint for QHD mode; blush for THE CATCH; marigold accent for Hz numbers
assets: assets_sources.md (A–J official Samsung images, K–L official product-page clips)
new_objects: frameStrip (film strip of frame cells scrolling; speed set by `hz`, labels per cell), pixelGrid (two grids side by side: 1280×720 drawn as 1 big cell per 4 small QHD cells, highlights '¼'), monitorOutline (generic unbranded flat monitor on stand, `label` text under it) — add each to render/kit/OBJECTS.md. Reuse counter, dialScale/gauge, toggle, ruler, clockRing, priceTag, questionStamp, crossMark, scoreTable, bars.

scenes.anchor: Samsung just made a monitor that hits eleven hundred hertz!
scenes.image: J cut out centred 75% width, slight push-in
scenes.object: gauge needle whips from 60 to 1,100 Hz on a dial below the monitor (marigold), counter rolls 60→1,100
scenes.note: frame 1 = poster A: monitor + '1,100Hz' huge, readable instantly

scenes.object: questionStamp '?' slams next to the number

scenes.anchor: Meet the Odyssey G six. It's a twenty-seven inch gaming screen.
scenes.image: B (3/4) 70% centre, then C slides in small left, I side profile right (product row)

scenes.anchor: Get this. At eleven hundred hertz, each frame lasts under one millisecond.
scenes.image: G (screen edge close-up) right 50%; clip L ≤ 2 s inside the screen area
scenes.object: new frameStrip: cells scroll past fast, each cell stamped '0.91 ms'; small clockRing (stopwatch) with '< 1 ms'

scenes.anchor: Want sharper? Switch to Q-H-D, and you still get six hundred hertz.
scenes.image: clip K ≤ 3 s (Samsung's own 600Hz/1100Hz mode switch), then F 60%

scenes.anchor: Here's the catch. Eleven hundred only works at seven-twenty p.
scenes.object: label '1280×720' under '1,100Hz' with arrowPointer; crossMark on a small 'QHD' pill

scenes.anchor: That's a quarter of the pixels.
scenes.object: new pixelGrid: QHD 4×4 cells vs HD 2×2 cells (each HD cell = 4 QHD cells), counter '921,600 vs 3,686,400', big '¼'

scenes.anchor: And LG already lists eleven hundred, overclocked.
scenes.object: new monitorOutline right labelled 'LG 25G590B' (text only, no LG logo) with label '1,000Hz native · 1,100Hz O/C · 1080p'; small source chip 'LG.com'
priceTag swings in with '$ ???' + questionStamp; calendar page blank 'date: TBA'

scenes.anchor: By our score? Forty-two out of a hundred.
scenes.object: scoreTable bars fill: price 12.5/25, claim 6/20, new 8/15, lasts 7.5/15, catch 8/15, buy 0/10 → TOTAL 42

scenes.anchor: It's a wreck. For now, anyway. Wait for the price, unless you play shooters competitively.
scenes.object: k falls (WRECK end-card motion); pill '⏳ wait for price' then pill '✓ pro FPS players'

scenes.anchor: Be honest. Would you trade sharpness for speed?
scenes.object: scale tips between 'SHARP 600Hz' and 'FAST 1,100Hz'; ends on the frame-1 layout (gauge at 1,100)
